newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas rises with futures, cooler forecast.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas rises with futures, cooler forecast.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices rebounded Friday, rallying in late morning trade in pursuit of the rising futures, market sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices gained about five cents to the mid-$1.80s early and the low-$1.90s late, as NYMEX's Henry Hub April gas futures soared 11.3 cents to a session high of $1.999.

Also boosting prices were forecasts calling for a continuation of cooler-than-normal weather in the Northeast through next week. Below-normal temperatures are forecast for the northern two-thirds of the U.S.
In the East, New York city-gate prices began trading in the teens and then softened to about $2.10 shortly before nomination deadlines, down from Thursday's trading range around $2.20.
In the Appalachian region, prices ranged anywhere from the low-$1.90s to low-$2 area in choppy trade.
In the Midcontinent, prices edged up one cent to the mid-to-high $1.70s, with Demarcation quoted in the high-$1.70s to low-$1.80s.
Temperatures in the Midwest are forecast to remain mostly normal through early next week, with slightly above-normal temperatures expected in the southern plains.
In the Permian basin, gas prices were steady to higher in the high-$1.60s to mid-$1.70s, while Waha prices climbed into the mid-$1.70s to about $1.80.
Southern California border prices were talked mostly in the mid-to-high $1.70s, down about five cents on the day, as West Coast utilities cut some of their purchases for the weekend.
The 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California is still scheduled to restart around March 12 following repairs of a leak, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said.
